issues.legal_issue: An appellate court should not reverse an acquittal when the trial court adopted a possible view of the evidence and no substantial and compelling reason justifies interference.
material_facts: The trial court acquitted the accused, and the appellate court reversed that acquittal as to one accused while confirming the acquittals of the others.
The injured eyewitness gave clear and consistent evidence assigning separate acts to the accused, and the appellate court relied on wound certificates to convict the accused despite that testimony.
The Supreme Court found no valid reason for reversing the acquittal on the evidence relating to the murder charges.
issues.conclusion: The appellate court was not justified in reversing the acquittal where the trial court's view was a possible view and substantial and compelling reasons for interference were absent.
issues.legal_principle: An appellate court may review evidence underlying an acquittal, but the presumption of innocence is strengthened by acquittal and, where two views are possible, the view favouring the accused should be adopted. Interference may be justified where, among other things, the trial court's factual conclusion is palpably wrong, its legal view is erroneous, its approach is patently illegal, it has ignored or misread material evidence, or its decision risks a grave miscarriage of justice. The Court relied on Ramanand Yadav v. Prabhu Nath Jha, (2003) 12 SCC 606.

predicates.appeal_against_acquittal: The proceeding is an appeal seeking to disturb a trial court's acquittal.
predicates.trial_view_is_possible: The trial court adopted a view of the evidence that is reasonably available on the facts and circumstances.
predicates.no_substantial_compelling_reason: The appellate court has not identified a substantial and compelling reason, such as a palpably wrong conclusion or disregard of material evidence, for disturbing the acquittal.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an acquittal, a reasonably available trial-court view and the absence of a substantial and compelling reason mean that reversal of the acquittal is unwarranted.

issues.legal_issue: A person cannot be convicted of murder on the basis of another person's fatal acts where the evidence establishes neither that the person participated in those acts nor that the persons shared an intention to kill.
material_facts: The eyewitness testified that the accused assaulted her, while identifying other accused as the persons who assaulted the two deceased people.
The eyewitness did not attribute to the accused any assault on the deceased people or any instigation of the assaults on them.
The acts attributed to the accused were distinct and separately described.
The acquittals of the persons identified as having assaulted the deceased people were confirmed, and the courts found no common intention to commit the murders.
issues.conclusion: The murder conviction was set aside, and the accused was acquitted of the murder offence.
issues.legal_principle: The Court found no evidence connecting the accused to the deaths and no evidence establishing common intention to commit the murders. On that record, the murder conviction could not stand.

predicates.appeal_from_murder_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from a murder conviction.
predicates.no_fatal_act_attributed_to_accused: The evidence does not attribute to the accused an act causing either death or instigation of the fatal assaults.
predicates.no_common_intention_evidence: The evidence does not establish that the accused shared an intention with others to cause the deaths.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a murder conviction, the absence of an attributed fatal act and of evidence of shared intention means the murder conviction is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for causing grievous hurt may be upheld when credible direct evidence establishes that the accused inflicted the victim's grievous injuries.
material_facts: The injured eyewitness consistently testified that the accused struck her with a chopper.
The testimony was clear, cogent, and consistent with her first information, and the Court found no reason to reject it.
The victim sustained an incised wound to the head and a fracture to the forearm.
issues.conclusion: The conviction for causing grievous hurt was upheld. The sentence was modified by imposing a fine payable to the injured victim as compensation, in addition to the prison sentence.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the credible evidence of the injured eyewitness and the grievous injuries proved in the record to uphold the conviction under Section 326 of the Indian Penal Code.

predicates.appeal_from_grievous_hurt_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from a conviction for causing grievous hurt.
predicates.credible_injured_eyewitness_identificati: An injured eyewitness gives credible evidence identifying the accused as the person who assaulted the victim.
predicates.grievous_injury_proved: The evidence establishes that the victim sustained grievous injuries from the assault.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a grievous-hurt conviction, credible identification by an injured eyewitness together with proof of grievous injury means the conviction is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A period of imprisonment already undergone may be credited against the prison sentence imposed, with release ordered if no other matter requires detention.
material_facts: The accused had already undergone a period of imprisonment exceeding the prison sentence imposed for the grievous-hurt offence.
The Court stated that the accused was entitled to credit for the imprisonment already undergone and ordered release if he was not required in another matter.
issues.conclusion: The period of imprisonment already undergone was set off against the sentence, and the accused was to be released unless required in another matter.
issues.legal_principle: The Court allowed credit for imprisonment already undergone against the sentence it imposed; the judgment does not identify a statutory provision or earlier case for this direction.

predicates.prison_sentence_imposed: The court imposes a prison sentence in the proceeding.
predicates.prior_imprisonment_undergone: The convicted person has already undergone imprisonment that can be credited against the sentence.
predicates.no_other_detention_required: No other matter requires the convicted person to remain in custody.

issues.definition: When a prison sentence is imposed, prior imprisonment has been undergone, and no other matter requires detention, that prior imprisonment is credited and release is ordered.
